settings.heading: A small shop, six objects at a time
settings.text:
Grain and Gold is a one-person shop, run from the Netherlands. The idea is simple: most of what we buy for our homes is replaced far sooner than it should be. So instead of stocking thousands of things, we pick a handful, and only keep the ones that earn their place.

No warehouse, no showroom, no team of buyers. Just careful choices, honest descriptions, and someone who actually reads your email.
settings.image_note: Lifestyle image — the shelf at home, morning light

settings.heading: How we choose what to sell
settings.text:
We keep the range at six. Adding a seventh means one has to go, and that rule has saved us from a lot of mediocre products. Every piece comes from a workshop we can reach by train or a short flight, and we have met the people who make each one.

Before anything is listed we use it at home for three months — through daily washing, spills, and the kind of handling a shop photo never shows. If it chips, fades, or simply annoys us, it does not get listed. That is also why restocks sometimes take a few weeks: we would rather be out of stock than substitute a supplier quietly.

settings.title: Fewer, better
settings.body: Six products, no seasonal drops, no clearance rails. If we cannot explain why a thing exists in one sentence, we do not stock it.

settings.title: Makers we have met
settings.body: Every workshop is named on its product page. We visit before the first order and pay in full within fourteen days.

settings.heading: Three things we hold to
settings.lead: Not a mission statement. Just the rules we actually run the shop by.
